title: OJP • Load spike demo
description: Follow a request spike, successful-request latency, connection pressure and overload rejections. Slowest SQL is always visible. SQL metrics do not export a user identity. Standalone dashboard for Grafana 10+.

panels.title: Demo: spike → bounded connections → shedding → latency

options.content:
Compare the **request spike**, **successful-request p95**, and **overload rejections** on the same timeline. Connections stay within configured pool capacity; waiting borrowers indicate pool contention, not the admission queue length. These measurements show what happened, not a guarantee of stable latency.

Request volume is **completed executeQuery/executeUpdate RPCs**, including failures—not incoming attempts. Rejections are gRPC status **8** (OJP maps admission overload to this status; it can have other causes). **Query users are not exported**; SQL is grouped across users/databases. SQL text may contain sensitive literals. Missing telemetry is **No data**, not healthy zero. For short spikes, use an appropriately short Prometheus scrape interval; rate windows smooth the spike.

panels.title: 1 · Request spike — completed SQL RPCs / sec
panels.description: Completion rate for executeQuery and executeUpdate only, including rejected/failed calls. This is not an arrival-rate metric and can lag a spike while requests wait. Each instance remains separate.

panels.title: 2 · Does latency stay stable? — p95
panels.description: Successful executeQuery/executeUpdate RPC duration (status 0) includes server handling/waiting, not full client-observed latency. SQL execution duration is a separate recorder with no method, user or datasource label, so its population is not identical. Rejected calls do not artificially lower the successful-RPC percentile. Zero traffic leaves percentiles undefined. No fixed latency SLO is assumed.

panels.title: 3 · Load shedding — overload responses / sec
panels.description: RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (gRPC status 8) for the same SQL RPCs as the load chart. GrpcExceptionHandler.sendServerOverload uses this status for admission-control rejections. This is a status-based signal, not a dedicated shed counter; other causes can share status 8. Zero is derived only from observed RPC telemetry. Missing instrumentation remains No data.

targets.expr: sum by (job, instance) (rate(rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_count{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",rpc_system="grpc",rpc_service="com.openjproxy.grpc.StatementService",rpc_method=~"executeQuery|executeUpdate",rpc_grpc_status_code="8"}[$__rate_interval])) or on (job, instance) (0 * sum by (job, instance) (rate(rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_count{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",rpc_system="grpc",rpc_service="com.openjproxy.grpc.StatementService",rpc_method=~"executeQuery|executeUpdate"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: 4 · Connections stay bounded — active / maximum
panels.description: OJP-managed active connections versus configured pool maximum, separately by instance, pool and Hikari/XA type. This is not total database connection usage. Nonpositive/unlimited maxima are omitted. An unused pool type may have no series.

panels.title: 5 · Pool pressure — waiting borrowers
panels.description: Threads waiting to acquire a Hikari/XA connection. A contention signal, not the OJP admission queue depth or a direct count of throttled requests. Requests may wait before pool acquisition, so zero here does not prove no throttling.

panels.title: 6 · Slowest SQL — top 5 by mean latency
panels.description: Highest mean database execution time over the selected range, descending. Zero-execution statements are excluded; low-volume queries may rank highly. Full SQL labels may contain sensitive literals. User identity and datasource are NOT exported by the SQL recorder, so ownership cannot be shown or inferred; this groups the same SQL across users/databases on each instance.

targets.expr: topk(5, sum by (job, instance, sql_statement) (increase(ojp_sql_execution_time_milliseconds_sum{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}"}[$__range])) / (sum by (job, instance, sql_statement) (increase(ojp_sql_execution_time_milliseconds_count{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}"}[$__range])) > 0))
